correctness.rationale: All hypotheses, domains, derivatives and quantifiers reconstructed. The target logarithm has a boundary argument uniformly below pi/2, yielding starlikeness. A rationally positive four-term cosine majorant and a recurrence-certified alternating tail establish Re(phi(w)) >= phi(-|w|) to 17/50. Schwarz–Pick on omega(z)/z bounds |z omega'(z)| for arbitrary Schwarz functions; the resulting bound decreases in |omega(z)|, so the minimum is H(r) and equality is attained by omega(z)=z at z=-r. Exact rational endpoint inequalities and strict monotonicity prove the unique root and the optimality of the radius. The embedded standard-library verifier confirms 120 exact coefficient terms, rational inequalities, high-precision root, and 5000 finite spot checks; finite tests are explicitly not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Classical convexity radius is a canonical stability/geometric invariant of an established 2026 starlike class. The theorem completely identifies this sharp universal threshold and exact radial order for every radius through it, with a single extremizer. The target-specific real-part comparison and rigorous Schwarz–Pick optimization are substantive structure, not an arbitrary small-cutoff calculation or a repackaging of a coefficient inequality. Prior primary work studied coefficients, distortion in modulus, or separate convex subclasses. The precise invariant informs when all images are guaranteed convex.
